/exchanges.title: No-KYC Crypto Exchanges: Limits Without ID | DoNotKYC
/exchanges.description: Centralised crypto exchanges that let you trade without sending ID, with their no-KYC withdrawal limits, fees and blocked countries.
intro: Centralised exchanges give you order books, deep liquidity, futures and mobile apps. The ones below ask for no ID document under a stated limit. Some still ask for ID before you can trade, so read each listing.
They hold your funds while they are on the platform. Withdraw to your own wallet when you are done, and check the limit before depositing more than it allows.
faq: Can an exchange ask for ID later?
Yes. Most no-KYC tiers can trigger a check on large withdrawals or unusual activity, and policies change. Start small and keep only what you are trading on the exchange.

/dex.title: Decentralised Exchanges (DEX) Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/dex.description: Decentralised exchanges where you trade straight from your own wallet: no sign-up, no ID, you keep your keys.
intro: A decentralised exchange runs on smart contracts. You connect your own wallet and trade without an account, so there is no identity to give and nobody holds your coins.
You pay network fees on top of the trading fee, and you need to be comfortable with a wallet. Some front-ends block certain countries even though the contracts stay open.

/swaps.title: Instant Crypto Swaps Without an Account | DoNotKYC
/swaps.description: Swap one coin for another without an account or ID. Limits, fees and when each swap service may ask questions.
intro: Instant swap services convert one coin to another in a single step: you send coins to an address and receive the other coin in your wallet. No account is needed.
Their margin is built into the quoted rate. Some can pause a swap their risk checks flag and ask for information before releasing it: the listing says when.

/p2p.title: P2P Bitcoin Markets Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/p2p.description: Buy and sell bitcoin with other people by bank transfer or cash, with escrow and no ID.
/p2p.h1: P2P markets: buy crypto from people
intro: Peer-to-peer markets put you in touch with a buyer or seller. You pay the other person with a bank transfer, cash or another method they accept, and an escrow releases the coins once they confirm.
Your bank still sees a transfer to a named person. Reputation and escrow rules matter more here than fees: read them before your first trade.

/atms.title: Bitcoin ATMs With Low or No ID | DoNotKYC
/atms.description: Bitcoin ATM networks where you can buy with cash, and the amounts above which they ask for ID.
/atms.h1: Bitcoin ATMs with low or no ID
intro: Bitcoin ATMs sell crypto for cash. Some accept small purchases with a phone number only and ask for ID above a threshold set by the operator and local rules. Others ask for ID on every purchase: each listing says which.
ATM fees run several percent above the market price. They are most useful for small amounts when cash is what you have.

/bridges.title: Cross-Chain Bridges Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/bridges.description: Move crypto between blockchains from your own wallet, without an account or ID.
intro: Bridges move assets from one blockchain to another, straight from your wallet. They do not ask for identity, but they are a frequent target of hacks.
Prefer well-established routes, check the fees and the estimated time before confirming, and move large amounts in several steps.

/alternatives/binance.title: Binance Alternatives Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/alternatives/binance.description: Binance requires identity verification. These exchanges and DEXs let you trade spot and futures without sending ID.
intro: Binance asks every user to verify their identity before trading. If you used it for spot trading, altcoins or futures, the exchanges and decentralised exchanges below do the same job with no ID, or none below a limit.
Check each platform's limit and blocked countries before moving funds. Terms change, so read the platform's own page before you deposit.

/alternatives/coinbase.title: Coinbase Alternatives Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/alternatives/coinbase.description: Coinbase requires ID to buy crypto. Ways to buy bitcoin and other coins by card, bank transfer or cash without sending ID.
intro: Coinbase asks for an ID document before you can buy. If you used it to buy crypto with a card or a bank transfer, these platforms accept fiat with no ID or with only light checks.
Fiat purchases are where limits bite first: most of these platforms set a maximum amount without ID.

/alternatives/kraken.title: Kraken Alternatives Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/alternatives/kraken.description: Kraken requires identity verification to trade. Exchanges with a no-KYC tier and decentralised exchanges that need no ID.
intro: Kraken requires identity verification before you can deposit and trade. These exchanges and decentralised exchanges let you trade without an ID document.

/alternatives/kucoin.title: KuCoin Alternatives Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/alternatives/kucoin.description: KuCoin made identity verification mandatory. Where to trade altcoins without ID now.
intro: KuCoin made identity verification mandatory for new users. For altcoin trading without ID, these exchanges, decentralised exchanges and swap services are the closest replacements.

/alternatives/revolut.title: Revolut Crypto Alternatives Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/alternatives/revolut.description: Buy crypto by bank transfer or card without the identity checks of a banking app.
intro: Banking apps like Revolut tie every crypto purchase to your verified identity. These platforms let you buy by bank transfer, card or cash without an ID document, or with only light checks.

/alternatives/paypal.title: PayPal Crypto Alternatives Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/alternatives/paypal.description: Buy crypto by card without the identity verification PayPal requires.
intro: PayPal requires a verified identity to buy crypto, and the coins stay inside PayPal. These services sell crypto by card and send it straight to your own wallet, with no ID up to their limit.

/alternatives/crypto-com.title: Crypto.com Alternatives Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/alternatives/crypto-com.description: Crypto.com requires ID. Exchanges and card on-ramps that let you trade and buy with no or light ID checks.
intro: Crypto.com asks for identity verification before trading or buying. These exchanges and fiat on-ramps work with no ID document, or none below a limit.

/alternatives/robinhood.title: Robinhood Crypto Alternatives Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/alternatives/robinhood.description: Buy bitcoin without the identity checks of a brokerage app: P2P markets, ATMs and swaps.
intro: Brokerage apps like Robinhood require your identity and keep your coins. If you want to buy bitcoin and hold it yourself, these P2P markets, ATMs and swap services are simpler and ask for little or no ID.

/buy/bitcoin.title: Buy Bitcoin Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/buy/bitcoin.description: Where to buy bitcoin without ID: P2P markets, ATMs, Lightning swaps and exchanges with no-KYC tiers.
intro: The most private ways to get bitcoin are peer-to-peer markets and small ATM purchases with cash. Exchanges with a no-KYC tier and swap services work if you already hold another coin.
Withdraw to a wallet you control as soon as the purchase is done.

/buy/monero.title: Buy Monero (XMR) Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/buy/monero.description: Where to get Monero (XMR) without ID: P2P trading and instant swaps that support XMR.
intro: Many large exchanges have delisted Monero, so you buy XMR peer to peer or swap it from another coin. These platforms support XMR without asking for ID.

/pay/cash.title: Buy Crypto With Cash, No ID | DoNotKYC
/pay/cash.description: Buy crypto with cash: Bitcoin ATMs and P2P markets that accept cash, and how much you can buy without ID.
intro: Cash leaves no bank record. You can use it at Bitcoin ATMs, which ask for ID above a threshold, or with sellers on P2P markets who accept cash in person or by mail.

/pay/bank-transfer.title: Buy Crypto by Bank Transfer Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/pay/bank-transfer.description: Buy crypto by bank transfer without sending ID to the platform, through P2P markets.
intro: A bank transfer is the cheapest way to buy, but your bank sees who you paid. On P2P markets you pay another person, so the platform does not ask for ID; the seller sees your name on the transfer.

/pay/card.title: Buy Crypto by Card Without KYC | DoNotKYC
/pay/card.description: Buy crypto with a debit or credit card without ID, up to each service’s limit.
intro: Card purchases are fast but rarely anonymous: card processors run their own checks, and limits without ID are low. These services accept cards with no ID up to their limit.

/cards.title: Crypto Cards and the ID They Ask For | DoNotKYC
/cards.description: Crypto cards you fund with crypto, and the identity checks each one asks for before you can spend.
/cards.h1: Crypto cards and their ID checks
intro: A crypto card is a Visa or Mastercard card you fund with crypto and spend wherever the network is accepted.

Nearly all of them check your identity, because the companies that issue cards answer to regulators. Each listing quotes what the card's own pages say about ID, and says so when they are unclear. Check fees, limits and country support before you load money.

methodology.title: How we check no-KYC platforms | DoNotKYC
methodology.description: How DoNotKYC lists crypto platforms: the identity levels, where the facts come from and when we update or remove a listing.
methodology.html:
How we check platforms

Every listing answers one question first: how much identity does this platform ask for, and when? Below: how we get that answer.

DoNotKYC is a community project built and maintained by Marlodevfs. The code and every change are public on GitHub.

The three identity levels

  • None: no ID document and no account details. You connect a wallet or trade without signing up.
  • Light: no ID under a stated limit, or only an email address or a phone number.
  • Tiered: an ID document is required above a threshold. The threshold is written on the listing.

Where the facts come from

Each listing is built from the terms, FAQ and help pages the platform publishes. When we have a source page for the identity level, the listing links to it.

We do not test platforms with real money. Policies change, and a platform can apply checks that no page announces. Treat every listing as a starting point, confirm it with the platform and do your own research before you send funds.

When a listing changes

If a platform makes ID mandatory for its core features, we re-tag or remove it. A platform that closes or is reported as a scam stays visible with that status, so people searching for it find the warning.

We check reports from users before changing anything. Submit a platform or report a change.

What you cannot buy

Listing, identity level and position in the directory cannot be bought. Some "Visit" links are affiliate links, and the page says so. Sponsored placements sit in separate tiles labelled as advertising.

submit.title: Submit a no-KYC platform | DoNotKYC
submit.description: Suggest a crypto exchange, swap, P2P market or ATM that lets people trade without sending ID, or report a listing that changed.
submit.html:
Submit a platform

Know a crypto platform that lets people trade without sending ID? Tell us. Listing is free, nobody can buy it, and advertisers get no faster review.

Open the submission form{icon}

What we check before listing

  • The platform's own terms, FAQ or help pages state its KYC policy and limits. A link to that source is required.
  • The site works, and its policy matches what users report.
  • No credible reports of exit scams, frozen funds without reason, or fake volume.
  • The identity level (None, Light or Tiered) fits the platform without guesswork.

A listing is wrong or out of date

If a listed platform now asks for ID, changed its limits or fees, blocks new countries or closed, report the change. We check every report before we update a listing.

Privacy

Both forms are public GitHub issues and need a GitHub account. Do not include personal data, and remove names or account numbers from screenshots. If a GitHub account is a problem, message us on Telegram.

Want to advertise instead?

Sponsored placements sit apart from listings and carry a label. See how advertising works.

advertise.title: Be featured on DoNotKYC | Sponsored placements
advertise.description: Reach people who already avoid KYC. Labelled sponsored tiles, reviewed advertisers. Free for now in exchange for a mention of DoNotKYC on your site.
advertise.html:
Be featured on DoNotKYC

DoNotKYC is read by people who want to trade crypto without handing over their identity. A sponsored tile puts your service next to the platforms they compare, with a Sponsored label.

Contact us on Telegram{icon}

Free for now, in exchange for a mention

We will publish prices once we have 30 days of audience figures. Until then a tile costs nothing. In return, your site shows that DoNotKYC features you, with a link to donotkyc.com, for as long as the tile runs. Your readers see where you are listed, and ours see you.

  • Write "Featured on DoNotKYC" (or "Sponsored placement on DoNotKYC").
  • Put it on your home page or on a page your visitors reach from it, with a normal link to donotkyc.com.
  • We check the mention before the tile goes live. If it disappears, the tile comes down.

Placements

  • Homepage tile: one sponsor at a time, in the "Where we would start" section.
  • Topic page tile: one sponsor per page, above the list. Pages include Exchanges, Decentralised exchanges, Instant swaps, P2P markets, Bitcoin ATMs, Bridges, Bitcoin, Monero, Cash, Bank transfer, Card.

The rules

  • Every tile says "Sponsored" and links with rel="sponsored".
  • Paying does not change a listing, its identity level or its position in the directory.
  • We review every advertiser before accepting. We refuse services with credible scam or frozen-funds reports, and anything illegal where it is offered.
  • We can remove a tile if new evidence of harm to users appears. Conditions are agreed before the tile goes live.

How it works

  1. Send us your service, the placement you want and the dates on Telegram.
  2. We review the service and reply.
  3. We agree the dates and where your mention goes.
  4. The tile goes live on the start date and comes down on the end date.

how-we-make-money.title: How DoNotKYC makes money | DoNotKYC
how-we-make-money.description: Affiliate links and labelled sponsored tiles pay for DoNotKYC. Neither changes a listing. Our advertising rules in full.
how-we-make-money.html:
How DoNotKYC makes money

DoNotKYC is a community project built and maintained by Marlodevfs. The code and every change are public on GitHub. DoNotKYC is free to read, with no paywall. It earns money in three ways, and none changes a listing.

Affiliate links

Some "Visit" buttons are affiliate links: if you sign up through one, the platform pays us part of its fees. You pay nothing extra. These platforms currently have one: {AFFILIATES}. In the VPN guide, the NordVPN and Proton VPN links are affiliate links too.

Affiliate links carry rel="sponsored". A platform with an affiliate link gets no better identity level, position or description than one without.

Sponsored tiles and advertising policy

A company can pay for a tile on the homepage or on a topic page. Every tile says "Sponsored", sits apart from the ranked list and links with rel="sponsored".

  • Paying never changes a listing, its identity level or its position. The same goes for the tools pages: a sponsor never buys a place on them.
  • We review every advertiser before accepting and refuse services with credible scam or frozen-funds reports.
  • We remove a tile if new evidence of harm to users appears.
  • We do not track visitors for advertisers: no cookies, no pixels.
  • Running sponsors are listed on the Be featured page.

Donations

You can support the project with a coffee on Buy Me a Coffee. A donation buys nothing: no listing, rank or review changes.

What we do not sell

  • Rankings, reviews or "verified" badges.
  • Visitor data. We never sell it, and the site counts visits without cookies: see the privacy policy.
  • The removal of a listing or of a warning.

Who decides the order

Platforms are sorted by how much identity they ask for, following our methodology. Anyone can point out an error in public on GitHub: report a change.

privacy-policy.title: Privacy policy | DoNotKYC
privacy-policy.description: DoNotKYC sells no data and keeps no personal data about you. No cookies, and one cookie-free visit counter. What GitHub Pages logs and what stays on your device.
privacy-policy.html:
Privacy policy

DoNotKYC does not sell data and keeps no personal data about you.

What the site does not use

  • No advertising trackers, no cookies.
  • Fonts, images and code come from www.donotkyc.com. The only outside script is the visit counter below.
  • Nothing you type on this site is sent to us. Submissions and corrections go through GitHub, under GitHub's own privacy statement.

What stays on your device

If you switch between light and dark theme, your browser remembers the choice in local storage. Site search also runs in your browser: your queries go nowhere.

Visit counter

We count visits with GoatCounter, an open-source counter that uses no cookies. It records which page was opened, the referring site, browser, country and screen size, never your name or anything that follows you across sites. We use it to know how many people read the site.

Hosting

The site runs on GitHub Pages. GitHub logs the IP address of visitors for security purposes. We have no access to those logs. GitHub's explanation.

Links to other sites

When you follow a platform link, you leave DoNotKYC and that site's policy applies. An affiliate link tells the platform you came from us; it tells us nothing about you. See how we make money.

Changes

Changes to this policy appear in the changelog. Last updated 19 October 2026.

about.title: About and contact | DoNotKYC
about.description: DoNotKYC is a community project run by Marlodevfs and khalil-xmr. What the site does, how it is funded and how to reach us.
about.html:
About and contact

DoNotKYC is a community project, not a company. Marlodevfs and khalil-xmr run it. The code and every change are public in the GitHub repository, and anyone can propose a fix.

What the site does

It lists crypto platforms and privacy tools and says plainly what each one asks of you: no identity, an account, or an ID. Facts come from the official site of each service, with a link to the source when we have one. How we check explains the levels.

How it is funded

Affiliate links and labelled sponsored tiles. Neither changes the order of a list or what a listing says. The details are on How we make money.

Your data

No accounts, no cookies, no forms. Visits are counted without tracking. See the privacy policy.

Contact us

  • A platform is missing: submit it on GitHub.
  • A fact is wrong or outdated: report a change.
  • Question, partnership or advertising: message @donotkyc55 on Telegram.
  • Security problem: use Telegram as well, and keep technical details out of public issues.

We have no contact email for now.

What we do not do

We give no financial or legal advice. No platform can pay for a better rank, a review or a "verified" badge.
